body.content: Exploring the pigeonhole principle on grids: For a 3x3 grid (9 points), there are 8 lines of 3 points. For a 4x4 grid (16 cells), selecting 13 points means omitting 3. To break all rows, columns, and diagonals of length 3, we need to omit at least 4 points (one for each row, one for each column, etc.). Thus, a 4x4 cell-center approach is structurally incapable of avoiding collinear triples.
body.why_keep_this: This proves that simple grid-based cell-center placements cannot work for 13 points and motivates the need for irregular perturbations or non-grid geometries.
